applies_why: The judge text decides Matthew 1:16 against a multi-verse answer and relies on no cited text stating the contrary in its own words, so it is doing the chain-vs-chain inquiry the rule governs.
quote: D1 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words': I weighed whether the judge may decide by the absence of an express contrary verse or must weigh the whole chain by footing; the judge used the former.
why: It declares Matthew 1:16 underdetermined because neither side's text states the contrary in its own words, rather than weighing the defender's cited verses as a chain by footing.
